title: Deterministic Policy-Constrained Remediation Engine
purpose: Capture the highest-leverage next architectural capability so the workspace can return to it later without prematurely implementing mutation or rollback behavior.

problem_statement.current_state: The workspace can validate, report, catalog, and prove runtime integrity, but it cannot yet compile or execute bounded compliant changes from failures or explicit intents.
problem_statement.architectural_gap: The system lacks a deterministic remediation layer that can transform governed state under policy instead of only observing and reporting on it.
problem_statement.target_shift: Evolve inf.work from a governance and introspection product into a governance-guided planning and bounded self-healing product.

what_it_changes: Introduces a first-class planning layer between validation and workspace mutation.
Turns stable rule failures and governed intents into deterministic remediation plans.
Adds bounded change execution semantics with verification and rollback contracts.
first_release_owns: Plan-only remediation from existing rule failures.
Dry-run simulation for governed JSON and derived artifact domains.
Structured provenance for planned and simulated remediation flows.
first_release_excludes: Freeform source-code synthesis or arbitrary workspace edits.
Open-ended natural-language execution without a supported strategy binding.

core_domain_objects.name: RemediationStrategy
core_domain_objects.role: Declares applicability, preconditions, allowed operation types, verification contract, rollback contract, and stable selection priority.

core_domain_objects.name: RemediationPlan
core_domain_objects.role: Immutable compiled plan containing objective, evidence, ordered operations, predicted impacts, verification steps, and rollback steps.

core_domain_objects.name: PlanOperation
core_domain_objects.role: Typed bounded action such as updating a JSON value, appending an index entry, regenerating governed artifacts, or running a validation profile.

core_domain_objects.name: VerificationContract
core_domain_objects.role: Defines the exact rules, tests, or profiles that must succeed after remediation.

core_domain_objects.name: RollbackContract
core_domain_objects.role: Defines how each operation can be deterministically reversed or restored from pre-state.

core_domain_objects.name: ChangeProvenanceRecord
core_domain_objects.role: Records intent, triggering evidence, selected strategy, executed operations, verification results, and final outcome.

engine_phases.description: Accept a trigger from failed rules or an explicit governed objective.
Gather affected surfaces using the resolver graph, component metadata, and governed indices.
Choose the deterministic winning strategy from a registry of supported remediation strategies.
Build an ordered immutable remediation plan with declared operations and verification requirements.
Produce dry-run diffs and a predicted post-state without mutating the workspace.
Execute only allowed bounded operations when the capability is later enabled.
Run the exact verification contract attached to the plan.
Emit provenance and either commit the successful plan or roll back deterministically.

already_present: Stable `rule_id`, severity, category, and profile mechanics in `src/inf_work/rules.py`.
Deterministic resolver traversal and bounded route validation in `src/inf_work/resolver_registry.py`.
Canonical JSON-first system snapshot generation and validation in `src/inf_work/system_status.py`.
Governed component metadata and KB cross-reference validation.
Focused and aggregate validation flows that can be reused as verification contracts.

ready_now: dry-run structured remediation for governed JSON and derived artifacts
impact analysis using existing resolver and component metadata
not_safe_yet: rollback-backed execution without typed operation contracts

safety_gates.description: Identical governed state and identical objective must compile to the same remediation plan.
Operations must target an explicitly allowed governed file class.
A strategy may compile only when all declared predicates pass.
No executable operation is allowed without a corresponding rollback contract.
A remediation is unsuccessful unless its attached verification contract passes after execution.
Every planned or executed remediation must emit structured audit data first.

minimum_first_slice.goal: Compile deterministic remediation plans for governed artifact and KB/index drift without mutating source files.

rollout_phases.name: Plan-only remediation
rollout_phases.outcome: Generate deterministic remediation plans from rule failures with no workspace mutation.

rollout_phases.name: Dry-run structured remediation
rollout_phases.outcome: Simulate JSON and derived-artifact changes with predicted diffs and verification contracts.

rollout_phases.name: Applied structured remediation
rollout_phases.outcome: Execute bounded governed-file operations with rollback and verification.

rollout_phases.name: Bounded source-level strategies
rollout_phases.outcome: Allow strategy-authored source edits only after typed operation and rollback semantics exist.

rollout_phases.name: Intent-driven governed change
rollout_phases.outcome: Support explicit capability requests, not only failure repair.

prerequisites_before_implementation: Define a typed `PlanOperation` vocabulary for structured changes.
Define rollback semantics per allowed operation type.
Create a deterministic remediation-strategy registry keyed by stable triggers.
Add a structured provenance artifact for plans and outcomes.
Define an explicit mutation policy for which governed file classes remediation may touch.

return_path.recommended_starting_point: Begin later with the minimum first slice: a plan-only remediation compiler for status artifact drift.
return_path.recommended_non_goal: Do not begin with arbitrary code-edit execution or generalized autonomous source mutation.
return_path.review_prompt: What is the smallest deterministic remediation slice that adds planning value without introducing unsafe mutation?
